conditions.displayName: work has been overdue for 15 minutes
overdue-work reporting stopped — absence is not health

documentation.content:
Scheduled work on the inflect-compliance VM is overdue: rows whose own
scheduling column says they are late, grouped by family.

WHY THIS EXISTS (#3558, caused by #3554). From 2026-10-07T09:09Z to
2026-10-14T20:30Z, `control-test-scheduler` claimed each due plan, failed to
enqueue the runner, rolled the claim back and retried — about 4,300 times, 24
an hour, for 7 1/2 days. ZERO scheduled control tests ran. It was found by a
human grepping logs for an unrelated reason.

Every signal that should have carried it worked: the failure counter was
incremented AND error-logged on every attempt, the tick logged "job completed"
each time (truthfully — having enqueued nothing), /api/readyz stayed green
because the process was healthy and only the work failed, and a manual trigger
worked because it passes no custom job id.

WHAT TO DO. The journal entry for the firing run names which rows are late:

    journalctl -u work-overdue-reporter.service -n 50

| family | means |
|---|---|
| control_test_plan | an ACTIVE plan's nextRunAt is >15 min in the past. The scheduler is not claiming, or claims and cannot enqueue (#3554's shape). |
| audit_outbox | PENDING entries with nextAttemptAt >15 min past. The audit flusher is not draining — compliance-relevant. |
| notification_outbox | PENDING mail with sendAfter >30 min past. Nobody is being emailed. |

Grace periods are 3x each flusher's cron cadence, so two consecutive missed
runs plus margin are needed. A guard test derives them from SCHEDULED_JOBS and
fails if a cadence change leaves a grace behind.

THE ABSENCE ARM IS NOT DECORATION. The reporter exits WITHOUT posting if any
query is unreadable, because an unreadable backlog is not an empty one —
posting 0 on a failed read would be a confident all-clear. Sustained silence is
therefore a real condition and this policy pages on it.

NOT COVERED: FAILED rows (work abandoned rather than not progressing), and the
~25 other SCHEDULED_JOBS entries that write no row a reporter can read, because
`runJob` persists no job-run history. That is the larger half of #3558.
